claims.text: CALPHAD-based computational thermodynamics can accurately predict melting temperatures of high-entropy alloys.
CALPHAD-based computational thermodynamics can accurately predict enthalpies of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
CALPHAD-based computational thermodynamics can accurately predict entropies of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
CALPHAD-based computational thermodynamics can accurately predict volume changes at melting of high-entropy alloys.
CALPHAD-based computational thermodynamics can accurately predict liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys.
The proposed calculations use alloy composition, temperature range, and a thermodynamic database as key inputs.
The thermodynamic database is the structural mediator of the proposed approach.
The predictions are generated through Gibbs free-energy minimization.
The approach applies to high-entropy alloys containing three to six principal elements.
The applicable temperature range is 298–2000 K.
The expected mean absolute error in melting temperature is less than 50 K.
The expected mean absolute error in enthalpy of fusion is less than 10 J/g.
The expected mean absolute error in entropy of fusion is less than 0.1 J/(g·K).
Literature experimental measurements are the baseline for evaluating the calculations.
Prediction uncertainty arises from the thermodynamic database and uncertainty in alloy composition.
The approach is to be falsified if melting-temperature error exceeds 100 K or fusion-enthalpy error exceeds 20 J/g for more than 20% of the tested alloys.
